content: CCR9, also known as C-C chemokine receptor type 9, is a protein encoded by the CCR9 gene in humans. This receptor has also been designated as CDw199, which stands for cluster of differentiation w199. The protein encoded by the CCR9 gene belongs to the beta chemokine receptor family. Structurally, it is predicted to be a seven-transmembrane protein, similar to G protein-coupled receptors. Chemokines and their receptors play a critical role in regulating the migration and maturation of thymocytes under both normal and inflammatory conditions. The specific ligand for CCR9 is CCL25. Research has shown that the CCR9 gene is differentially expressed in T lymphocytes located in the small intestine and colon. This suggests that CCR9 may be involved in the recruitment and development of thymocytes, potentially allowing for functional specialization of immune responses in distinct regions of the gastrointestinal tract. The CCR9 gene is located within the chemokine receptor gene cluster region. Additionally, two alternatively spliced transcript variants of this gene have been identified.
